A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same extraction pipeline, dataset, and analyses despite the changed title. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluation of extraction quality, annotation-time measurements, and quantitative analyses of prompting results (§§3–4 and Appendix C).

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds analyses restricted to peer-reviewed publications (§4.5 and Appendix C.3).

M1.justification: The filtering, schema-driven extraction, context augmentation, and dataset-description procedures remain unchanged, as do the appendix prompts. Specifying Llama3.1-70B-Instruct and describing decoding settings clarify implementation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds a test scenario restricted to peer-reviewed publications, examining a selected population of studies (§4.5 and Appendix C.3). The underlying 18,127-record corpus, four target models, and task categories remain unchanged; coding was already covered in v1.

E2.justification: Comparisons remain CoT versus direct prompting, few-shot versus zero-shot, and more versus fewer demonstrations, including in the filtered analyses. No new extraction baseline is evaluated; newly cited systems are not experimental comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces selection using DBLP publication metadata for the peer-reviewed reanalyses. Existing matching constraints, metrics, collection period, and 40-record human evaluation remain unchanged. The added decoding description does not establish a revision to an earlier experimental setting.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused robustness check asking whether CoT task benefits and CoT–ICL interactions persist after restricting publication status (Table 7 and Appendix C.3, Tables 8–9). Existing negative-case and demonstration-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The one-sided bootstrap and Bonferroni threshold of 0.00227 already appear in v1 Appendix C and Table 7. v2 reuses these procedures and existing quartile reporting for filtered results, without adding run counts, seeds, or a new uncertainty estimator.

E6.justification: v2 adds filtered results, including mean CoT deltas of 13.53 for math and 9.13 for symbolic reasoning, and demonstration-benefit medians of 5.0. Multi-hop and context-aware QA lose significance in that subset. Original Table 7 values remain as Total Results. Existing plot medians change from 1.9 to 1.3 in Figure 5, 1.9 to 1.4 in Figures 6/8, and 1.8 to 2.0 in Figure 7, without explained causes. Main trends remain stable.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. Performance-delta definitions and metric normalization are retained. Appendix B's added rationale for averaging rating scores does not introduce a mathematical derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the highlighted ICL-benefit claim from multimodal tasks to coding and multimodal tasks. The abstract also specifies zero-shot CoT as the comparison for limited math gains. Core extraction, efficiency, scalability, and CoT–ICL interaction claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets agreement with the peer-reviewed subset as evidence of robustness, generalizability, and hypothesis confirmation (§4.5 and Appendix C.3). This interpretation is new, although some secondary significance findings differ. The negative-case explanations and substantive limitations in §7 remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly describes default generation settings with greedy decoding, limited hyperparameter tuning, and prompt-development choices. v2 specifies the Instruct filtering model and adds a dedicated Hugging Face dataset access link alongside the existing code link.

R1.justification: v2 adds Frankston et al. (2024) and Wang et al. (2024, CharXiv) when motivating LaTeX extraction, and Kim et al. (2023, Prometheus) when supporting the rating rubric. Positioning relative to extraction systems and Sprague et al. remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, names the dataset LLMEVALDB, replaces meta-analysis terminology with literature analysis, and revises portions of the abstract, introduction, and explanations. It adds §4.5 and Appendix C.3 while retaining the main section order and much existing prose.

P2.justification: Table 7 moves from the appendix to the main text and gains Total/Filtered columns; new Tables 8–9 juxtapose original and filtered interaction results. Existing plots receive revised titles, axes, legends, and formatting. The overall two-column layout and pipeline illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens the paper through publication-status robustness checks and clearer implementation and dataset-access information. Table 7 and Appendix C.3 provide useful corroboration of central findings. Benefits are limited by unspecified filtered sample sizes and precise venue-selection rules, unexplained revisions to plot medians, and broad confirmation language that overlooks lost significance in some QA categories.
